precepts.text: Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight. David understood the Lord was with him in every fight and battle, and the Lord was teaching him how to fight. David chased a lion and killed it; he fought bears. How was he able to do that? The Lord was with him.
precepts.point: This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
David said to Goliath, “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel”. When we fight and when we war, we war in the name of our God. Then Psalm 144 shows where David's fighting came from: “Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight”.

This is David, and he says God is his strength, and it is God that teaches his hands to war. David understood that the Lord was with him in every fight and every battle he was in, and the Lord was the one teaching him how to fight. David didn't go to no kung fu school. The Lord was literally teaching David how to fight. David chased a lion and killed it; David was fighting with bears. How was he able to do that? The Lord was with him.

“and my fingers to fight”: and my fingers to punch a dude and break his teeth. Y'all don't be doing that to nobody today, unless you are defending yourself.

So the Lord is our strength, brothers. Always remember that. That is how you learn to war and fight: the Lord is with you, and you can't war without the Lord warring with you. That is why David could tell the Philistine, “This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand”, “that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel”, and that “the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s”. Anytime you go to war, it's the Lord that's with you fighting.

precepts.text: When the Philistines spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim, David enquired of the Lord. David used to talk to the Lord before he made decisions, and we have to learn to do that: Lord, should I do this? If it is not right, shut it down. The Lord said, Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees. And when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines. The Lord goes out before you, fighting with you. And when you read the Maccabees, angels came down and fought with Judas Maccabeus too.
precepts.point: This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.” “And when David enquired of the Lord”: David sought counsel of the Lord. David used to talk to the Lord: Lord, should I go up now? Should I do this? Should I do that?

We have to learn to do that. Before you make a decision, talk to the Lord: I want to do this, but show me what's right, show me should I do this or not; and if it's not right, Lord, shut it down. Sisters, do that when you are marrying some of these brothers: Lord, if this brother ain't right, shut it down. Brothers, do that too: Lord, if this sister is a demon, make me see it. You can talk to the Lord. He does hear you; you are not talking to yourself.

The Lord answered, “Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” Don't go up right now; go around them and come up behind them, behind the mulberry trees. This goes back to the Lord teaching David how to war.

“And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.” See in your mind what is taking place: when you hear me running on top of the mulberry trees, the Lord running on top of the trees, then rush yourself. I am going out before you. I'm there fighting with you, David, and we are going to smite the host of the Philistines.

That is the wars of the Lord, and it is what David meant before Goliath: “for the battle is the Lord’s, and he will give you into our hands.” The Lord goes out before his people and fights with them. When you read the Maccabees, angels came down and fought with Judas Maccabeus too, shielding him so nobody could hit him.

precepts.text: The Most High hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind; the fear in the camp was not his spirit.
precepts.point: The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle, and this fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith; the same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them, and a trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
Goliath cried unto the armies of Israel, “choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.” If he kills me, we will be your servants; if I prevail and kill him, ye shall be our servants. “I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.” “When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.”

They were in a carnal spirit, measuring his height, his armor and his reach. The spirit had departed, and fear is not the spirit of the Most High: “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” The fear in the camp was not his spirit.

precepts.text: I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die? The chosen people of the living God have no business fearing a man who will be made as grass.
precepts.point: The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle, and this fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith; the same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them, and a trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
“I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass”. The chosen people of the living God have no business fearing a man who will be made as grass.

A trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth, and they were dismayed.

precepts.text: When thou goest out to battle and seest a people more than thou, be not afraid of them, for the Lord thy God is with thee; the priest was to tell the people, let not your hearts faint, fear not, for the Lord your God goeth with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.
precepts.point: The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle, and this fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith; the same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them, and a trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle: “When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” The priest was to tell the people, “let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble, neither be ye terrified because of them; For the Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.”

This fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith. The same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them.

precepts.text: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? That is the spirit the Most High looks for, one who will stand up for his people against the workers of iniquity; he is not worried about outward appearance.
precepts.point: This is why the Most High said in chapter 16 that he had refused David's brothers: they were there and did not have the spirit to rise up; they were among the ones who fled.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
David rose early, left the sheep with a keeper, and came to the trench as the host was shouting for the battle. While he saluted his brethren, the champion came up “and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.” The same daily smack talk.

“And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.” Think on it: the whole nation’s freedom, everything they possessed, was on the line, and they ran scared. This is why the Most High said in chapter 16 that he had refused David’s brothers. They were there and did not have the spirit to rise up; they were among the ones who fled.

“Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” That is the spirit the Most High looks for, one who will stand up for his people against the workers of iniquity. He is not worried about outward appearance.

precepts.text: That I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel; the Most High calls his people, the children of Israel, his armies.
precepts.point: The soldiers themselves did not understand that they were the armies of the living God; David, a sheep keeper sent on an errand, knew it. Israel is the army of the Most High, and every army requires order; that is why there are captains and officers, and despising that order is despising the army of the living God.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
David asked, “What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”

The soldiers themselves did not understand that they were the armies of the living God; David, a sheep keeper sent on an errand, knew it. The Most High said it in Egypt: “that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” He calls his people, the children of Israel, his armies.

Israel is the army of the Most High, and every army requires order. That is why there are captains and officers, and despising that order is despising the army of the living God.

precepts.text: Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjathsepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife; the same kind of offer the king made over Goliath.
precepts.point: The soldiers themselves did not understand that they were the armies of the living God; David, a sheep keeper sent on an errand, knew it. Israel is the army of the Most High, and every army requires order; that is why there are captains and officers, and despising that order is despising the army of the living God.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
The men of Israel said, “the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.” A prize was on Goliath’s head.

Caleb made a like offer: “He that smiteth Kirjath–sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.” The same kind of offer the king made over Goliath.

precepts.text: Let no man despise thy youth, but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity; the nation had no example of faith that day, so a young youth had to be that example.
precepts.point: Young people coming into this truth: if the Most High is dealing with you in a special way, do not let anybody discourage you or tell you that you are too young to be a mighty man of the Lord. Do not let it deter you.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
David’s words were rehearsed before Saul, and David told him, “Let no man’s heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.” Nobody panic; I will handle it. Saul answered, “Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.”

“Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.” The nation had no example of faith that day, so a young youth had to be that example.

Young people coming into this truth: if the Most High is dealing with you in a special way, do not let anybody discourage you or tell you that you are too young to be a mighty man of the Lord. Do not let it deter you.

precepts.text: David played with lions as with kids and with bears as with lambs; he was a mighty young man, and Saul did not know that about him.
precepts.point: David said, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. Same God, no difference. And Saul said, Go, and the Lord be with thee.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
David gave Saul his resume. Keeping his father’s sheep, when “there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock”, he went out after him and delivered it out of his mouth, “and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him.” He might have looked small, but he was killing lions and bears behind his sheep.

“He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs.” David was a mighty young man, and Saul did not know that about him.

“The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.” Same God, no difference. “And Saul said unto David, Go, and the Lord be with thee.”

precepts.text: Above all taking the shield of faith, and the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God; David went to the battle believing his God would fight for him, carrying the word instead of carnal armor.
precepts.point: Instead of the helmet and the brass, David took his staff, chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, put them in a shepherd's bag, and took his sling in his hand. What he put on instead was the whole armour of God: the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the spirit.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
Saul armed David with his own armor: “he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.” David girded his sword upon it and assayed to go, “for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him.”

Instead of the helmet and the brass, David “took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd’s bag”, and “his sling was in his hand”. What he put on instead was the whole armour of God: “Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God”.

David went to the battle believing his God would fight for him, carrying the word instead of carnal armor.

precepts.text: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts; the only way Israel overcomes.
precepts.point: David understood he did not need the sword, the spear, or the shield; he had the spirit of the living God. It is no amount of carnal firepower that overcomes the enemies of Israel; this is spiritual warfare, and our forefather David understood that.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
When the Philistine saw David, “he disdained him: for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and of a fair countenance.” “Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves?” He cursed David by his gods and promised to give his flesh “unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.”

David answered, “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.” Again the record shows who the army of the Most High is: Israel.

David understood he did not need the sword, the spear or the shield; he had the spirit of the living God. “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” That is the only way Israel overcomes. It is no amount of carnal firepower that overcomes the enemies of Israel; this is spiritual warfare, and our forefather David understood that.

precepts.text: I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen; prophecy that Judah would be saved without carnal weapons.
precepts.point: All this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's. The Most High fights how he wants to fight, not how man thinks it must be done.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
The Lord said it long before: “I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen.” That is a prophecy that Judah would be saved without carnal weapons.

David spoke the same thing to Goliath's face: “the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s.” He prophesied the outcome before the fight, “This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand”, so “that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.”

The Most High fights how he wants to fight, not how man thinks it must be done. Judah is saved “by the Lord their God”, not by bow or by sword.

precepts.text: The fulfillment in Hezekiah's day: the angel of the Lord went out and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand, and Judah woke up to the battle already won; that is how the Lord gets down.
precepts.point: All this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's. The Most High fights how he wants to fight, not how man thinks it must be done.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
Here is the fulfillment in Hezekiah's day. The Lord said, “I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.” And that night “the angel of the Lord went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.”

Not one sword was lifted by Judah. They went to sleep and woke up to the battle already won. That is how the Lord gets down.

It is the same word David gave before he ever slung the stone: “the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s, and he will give you into our hands.”

precepts.text: David slew a giant when he was yet but young and took away reproach from the people; he called upon the Most High, and it was the Most High who gave his right hand strength to slay that mighty warrior.
precepts.point: When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled. They ran from a young youth because they knew something supernatural was going on; he was in the spirit of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
“Slew he not a giant, when he was yet but young? and did he not take away reproach from the people, when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat down the boasting of Goliath?” David was but a youth, and he took the reproach off of Israel.

Where did the strength come from? “For he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.” It was the Most High who gave David's right hand its strength.

That is why one shot was all it took. The stone left the sling with the velocity of a bullet, and it “sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.” David “prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone”, and “there was no sword in the hand of David.” He ran, stood upon the Philistine, drew Goliath's own sword “out of the sheath thereof”, and “cut off his head therewith.”

“And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.” They ran from a young youth because they knew something supernatural was going on: he was in the spirit of the Lord.

moments.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God. When you read verse 16 it tells you that Goliath presented himself for forty days. He would come out every day, call out Israel, talk smack. They had no challengers. He would go back. Tomorrow he would come out and do the same thing. For forty days he did this. So this is a progression, until the point where David presents himself right now.
So David is talking smack. He said, who is this uncircumcised Philistine defying the armies of the living God?

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: David said moreover, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. So now David is dropping his resume that no one knew about. David was killing lions and bears on the low. Imagine you are just walking one day on the dirt road and you see a lion torn up on the side. You are like, what happened to the lion? You see a bear mangled. What happened to the bear? David is sitting there with a bear skin coat on at the house. You do not know how he got it. You are thinking he bought it at the swap meet or the mall. Nah, he made that.

And Saul said unto David, Go, and the Lord be with thee. So once David dropped his resume, Saul was like, okay, I did see a couple of dead carcasses on the way here. Well, that was you. Okay, you know what, go ahead, do your thing, young man. Because David was a young man.

points: David asked, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine and taketh away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

The soldiers themselves did not understand that they were the armies of the living God; David, a sheep keeper sent on an errand, knew it. Israel is the army of the Most High, and every army requires order; that is why there are captains and officers, and despising that order is despising the army of the living God.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: Eliab, the eldest brother, heard David and his anger was kindled: why camest thou down hither, and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride and the naughtiness of thine heart; thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle. A big brother talking down to a little brother, accusing him of sneaking out to watch.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: David answered, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? The men are scared, nobody will step up; what is the problem? And he turned to another and spake after the same manner.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: David's words were rehearsed before Saul, and Saul sent for him. David told Saul, Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine. Nobody panic; I will handle it.

Young people coming into this truth: if the Most High is dealing with you in a special way, do not let anybody discourage you or tell you that you are too young to be a mighty man of the Lord. Do not let it deter you.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: Saul answered, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: David gave Saul his resume: keeping his father's sheep, when a lion and a bear took a lamb out of the flock, he went out after him, smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth; when he arose against him, David caught him by his beard and slew him. He might have looked small, but he was killing lions and bears behind his sheep.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: David said, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. Same God, no difference. And Saul said, Go, and the Lord be with thee.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: Saul armed David with his own armor, a helmet of brass and a coat of mail, and David girded his sword upon the armor and assayed to go; but he had not proved it, and he said, I cannot go with these, and put them off him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: Instead of the helmet and the brass, David took his staff, chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, put them in a shepherd's bag, and took his sling in his hand. What he put on instead was the whole armour of God: the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the spirit.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: When the Philistine looked about and saw David, he disdained him, for he was but a youth, ruddy and of a fair countenance: Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods and promised to give his flesh to the fowls of the air and the beasts of the field.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: David answered, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied. Again the record shows who the army of the Most High is: Israel.

David understood he did not need the sword, the spear, or the shield; he had the spirit of the living God. It is no amount of carnal firepower that overcomes the enemies of Israel; this is spiritual warfare, and our forefather David understood that.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: David prophesied the outcome before the fight: this day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand, and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: All this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's. The Most High fights how he wants to fight, not how man thinks it must be done.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: David hasted and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine, took a stone from his bag, slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the earth. David had precise aim and power; that stone left the sling with the velocity of a bullet, and it took one shot.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: David prevailed with a sling and with a stone, and there was no sword in the hand of David; he ran and stood upon the Philistine, drew Goliath's own sword out of the sheath, slew him, and cut off his head with it.
When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled. They ran from a young youth because they knew something supernatural was going on; he was in the spirit of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: When Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he asked Abner, the captain of the host, Whose son is this youth? And Abner could not tell; in the shock of it they forgot whose son the young man was.
That is the history of David and Goliath: when the mighty men of Israel ran afraid, a young youth stood up bold in the spirit of the Lord and took the giant down.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: As David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine with the head of the Philistine in his hand, Abner brought him before Saul, and David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear
